.qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r15/rules/projects/webdev-task-template/tests/{scoring.toml,tools/score.py,test.sh} (byte-compared with the task copies: identical), template scored/visual/judge.toml anchors
evidence:
STATIC RESULT: no weight, gate, floor or criterion arrangement that inverts the ranking was found. RUNTIME RESULT: reward ordering is not measured for these bytes, and none of the 22 artifacts in the raw evidence index could be verified because the files are absent. Details follow.

1) Aggregation (template-identical, diff of scoring.toml / score.py / test.sh against the frozen template is empty). tests/scoring.toml: '[gates] render = 0.0, constraints = 0.0', '[weights] functional = 0.6, polish = 0.2, visual = 0.2', '[floors] functional = 0.05'. tests/tools/score.py: 'gates_passed = all(scores[k] > floor ...)', 'weighted = sum(w * scores[k] ...) / sum(weights.values())', 'reward = round(weighted, 4) if gates_passed and floors_passed else 0.0'. All dimension weights are positive and every criterion weight is positive (functional 43 criteria, weight sum 59.0, range 1.0-2.0; polish 6 x 1.0; visual 3 likert x 1.0), so above the gates and floor the reward is non-decreasing in every criterion: passing one more criterion can never lower it. Function (0.6) outweighs polish plus visual (0.4), so the skill's example 'craft carrying more mass than function' does not apply.

2) Gates do not exclude a stronger app on something the brief leaves open. gates/render/judge.toml cw_workspace_loads_and_takes_typing asks only for load, typing and reload ('Do not press Run, do not save anything and do not judge any other feature here'), so an app with a broken Run is no longer zeroed at the gate (the index records that an earlier candidate zeroed a model there: 'render gate failed because Run never works in its app'). The same load-and-type bar is the in-dimension gate of all three scored prompts, so gate and scored suites agree. gates/constraints cw_custom_document_surface enforces the public ui.md rule ('Don't use a textarea, input or contenteditable element as the document surface, and don't use CodeMirror, Monaco, Ace ...') and expressly allows the permitted alternative ('A small input or textarea that is used only to receive keyboard or clipboard events is allowed'); cw_shared_saved_record enforces integration.md ('The library must be shared between independent browser contexts', 'Use SQLite for persistent records') with one save and a read-back after clearing browser storage, which is what REVIEW_POLICY.md asks of a gate ('Use an actual successful operation and independent-context readback').

3) Criteria do not pay a dead feature for doing nothing. Every negative or refusal criterion carries a positive control that fails the criterion when absent: cw_dynamic_code_refused ('or if the harmless control draft is refused'), cw_preview_isolation ('treat a probe that stays silent as not performed, which fails this criterion'; 'if ordinary own-preview DOM and console activity did not work'), cw_stop_cancels_pending_work ('or if the control marker never appeared'), cw_newer_run_supersedes, cw_time_limit_recovery, cw_stale_save_refused ('or if A's control Save did not succeed'), cw_stale_save_keeps_draft ('or if B's Save was not refused'), cw_live_update_keeps_editing_state ('If A's library never shows B's snippet, this criterion fails as well'), cw_newer_revision_notice_keeps_draft (baseline), cw_format_error_keeps_draft ('or if the valid control did not format'), cw_restore_request_repeat_safe ('Fails if the first restore did not add the third revision'). app_context.md: 'a criterion whose steps need a working Run fails if Run does not work'. So an app with Run, Stop, Save or live refresh missing cannot collect the suppression/refusal credit that a working app has to earn.

4) Floor arithmetic. The floor needs more than 2.95 of 59.0 functional weight (strict '>'), i.e. about two to three criteria. Worst template-shape comparison: F=3/59, P=1, V=1 gives 0.4305 against F=0.7, P=0, V=0 giving 0.42. The first profile is not reachable here: five of six polish criteria need working Run feedback, Save, Format, Undo/Redo and Replace all (cw_controls_feedback_and_labels, cw_focus_returns_to_code, cw_undo_redo_availability, cw_unsaved_marker, cw_narrow_width_usable), which themselves earn functional credit, so polish cannot be farmed by a shell.

NOTES (not defects in this row):
(a) cw_controls_keyboard_and_focus says 'A control the app does not have at all is scored elsewhere, not here', so an app that omits Find/Replace passes this one polish criterion (1/6 x 0.2 = 0.033) while an app that has a Find control that cannot be reached by keyboard fails it. The omitting app loses at least 5.0/59 x 0.6 = 0.051 functional (four find/replace criteria) plus cw_focus_returns_to_code (0.033), so the order is preserved against an app whose Find/Replace works; against an app whose Find/Replace is present but dead the two are arguably equally weak and the gap is 0.033.
(b) An app with a strong editor and a broken Save scores 0 at cw_shared_saved_record while a thin app with a working Save scores above 0. This is the gate policy, backed by a public hard requirement, not an inversion.
(c) Visual uses 'type = "likert", points = 5' with a '0:' anchor and the prompt line 'Each criterion is scored from 0 to 5'. The only surviving hosted figure, 'visual: 0.9167' (scored/rewardkit.log line 3, earlier candidate), equals 11/12, which fits a (score-1)/4 normalisation; I could not confirm how a 0 is normalised (reward-details.json is absent). If it produced a negative dimension value, score.py would raise ('invalid RewardKit dimension') and test.sh would write a zero reward. A 0 is anchored only to 'no editor is shown', which cannot coexist with a passed render gate, and the frozen template uses 0 anchors too, so I record it as latent only.
(d) Grading time grows with how much of the app works (a working feature needs all its steps, a broken one is failed after two attempts: 'Fail fast'), and a scored-suite timeout leaves reward 0, so a timeout would hit the better app first. The index states the Oracle on an earlier 41-criterion candidate took 'about 42 minutes including all judges' against budgets of 9000 s (functional judge) and 11100 s (suite); that margin is not measured for these 43-criterion bytes.

EVIDENCE GAPS (reason for risk=true):
- raw-evidence-index.json lists 22 artifacts with SHA256 values. At review time (2 Oct 2026, about 20:30 IST) all 22 were missing from disk, so no hash could be verified: qc/repairs/coldwater-2026-10-02-strict contains only results/build.log and results/restart.log (no run_golden.sh, no tests/*.cjs, no results/*.json or *.png), and the hosted run directories contain only *.log files (no result.json, reward.json or reward-details.json). The parent directories carry a modification time of 20:27, after the index was written at 20:22.
- By the index's own scope line, 'No configured judge run exists for these bytes', and the scripted golden run covers only the golden. There is no run of weakened or mutated apps on these bytes, so the reward-ordering record that REVIEW_POLICY.md requires ('separate, hash-bound runtime records for ... reward discrimination and reward ordering') does not exist. The earlier hosted run (Oracle 0.9833, nop 0, model 0 at the gate) gives no ordering between partial apps, and its candidate differs.
